title: M0 Spike: render one Anth.us article page in a Lambda, byte-identical and timed
description:
## Outcome
Prove, before any build-out, that one Anth.us article page renders inside a Lambda in milliseconds and produces exactly the bytes the full build produces.

## Design
/Users/home/Projects/markus-publication-architecture-v2.md sections 1 (Measurements) and 10 (Spike).

## Checklist
- [ ] Test Lambda (Python 3.12, arm64, 2048 MB) packaged like content-actions (Markus 0.5.1, Pillow>=11.3, citeproc) plus Papyrus pin c98435f renderer and the Anth.us web/ modules
- [ ] Image metadata supplied as meta.json (or a copied rendition cache) so no image is decoded
- [ ] Render articles/agent-skills/index.html with Markus called in-process; PUT to a scratch bucket
- [ ] Record split: import/init, render, image metadata, PUT

## Acceptance (pass/fail)
- PASS: object bytes equal the local full build's file (sha256 equal) AND warm invoke (render + PUT) < 200 ms AND cold start < 2 s.
- FAIL: report the measured split and update v2 section 1.

## Out of scope
Any production resource, any template change, listings, renditions generation.

## Dependencies
None.

## Risk
Low. Scratch bucket and test function only (create in papyrus-staging or a sandbox with Ryan's yes).

## Estimate
1 agent-hour.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
M0 spike result (2026-10-12). Overall: PARTIAL. Parity and cold start pass; warm under 200 ms passes only after one design change, and not for the heaviest article. Epic left open for Ryan.

1. Bytes: PASS. sha256 equal for articles/agent-skills/, articles/maximize-profit-not-intelligence/ (18 images, 15 citations) and the /articles/ listing, against a cold full CMS-export build (Papyrus c98435f, Markus 0.5.1 in-process in the Lambda, subprocess in the reference). Condition: the version token had to be supplied. The reference build has two tokens: 8bfa91c69d80 on the 129 Markus pages and e10e352d5970 on the 68 generated pages, because it hashes assets/ including image renditions at different build stages. The Lambda cannot recompute that; M1 needs one deploy-time token.
2. Warm render+PUT under 200 ms: FAIL as built (median 411 ms agent-skills, 584 ms rich article, 407 ms listing; 360 ms is pure-Python YAML parsing of 129 front matters per invocation). With front matter pre-parsed (JSON, lossless for this corpus): 102 ms agent-skills (prepare 51, render 5, PUT 35), 98 ms listing, 235 ms rich article (render 110, prepare 85, PUT 39). So PASS for typical articles, FAIL for the citation-heavy one by ~35 ms.
3. Cold start under 2 s: PASS. Init 978 ms (Python imports 892 ms) across 4 cold samples (951-978 ms); first invoke adds 259 ms (agent-skills) to ~480 ms (rich; citeproc/CSL lazy imports), billed 1.24-1.47 s; client wall 1.66-2.0 s. YAML variant: Init 1261 ms, billed 1886 ms.
Package: 14.8 MB zip, 43 MB unzipped, 133 MB max memory at 2048 MB. Images: renditions assumed present; image metadata from precomputed size/alpha (no decode).
Cleanup done: stack papyrus-spike-m0 (bucket emptied first, only spike output) and its log group deleted, scratch dir and npm caches removed. Artifacts: /Users/home/Projects/.baselines/m0-spike-20261012/ (NOTES.md, handler, scripts, raw results).

right_now_summary: The Lambda spike will test byte-identical rendering and measure cold-start, render, and upload times.
